facts.text: Gantt sits on the west bank of the Conecuh River, where the Gantt Dam creates a lake that defines the town’s eastern boundary.
In the late 1800s, Gantt grew as a river‑based settlement that floated timber, turpentine, cotton, tobacco, and pecans to Pensacola.
The Central of Georgia Railroad arrived in 1899, prompting Gantt to relocate one mile east toward the tracks and spark industrial growth.
Gantt Dam, built in 1899, was followed by a 1920 hydroelectric plant that supplied the town’s first electricity, initially only at night.
The town’s name briefly changed to Christine, allegedly after a local schoolteacher, before settling on Gantt.
Early settlers from South Carolina, including the Gantts and Gunters, established homes along the Conecuh River in the mid‑1800s.
